NATO to Deploy Early-Warning Aircraft to Poland Following Russian Missile Incidents — NATO has agreed to provide Poland with an AWACS early-warning aircraft after three Russian Kh-101 missiles detonated on its territory. Other Polish requests to strengthen air defenses and deterrence will be discussed next week.

The attack followed a Russian strike on a private clinic in the city that killed three people on Monday.

Poland’s military authorized its destruction but withheld fire over concerns for civilian safety. The drone subsequently returned to Ukrainian airspace. The incident renewed concerns over repeated Russian airspace violations along NATO’s eastern flank.

Libya’s Tripoli Condemns Ukraine’s Strikes on Russian Ships — Libya’s UN-recognized government in Tripoli condemned Ukraine’s naval drone attacks on two Russian vessels near Benghazi, while the rival eastern administration called for a UN investigation into the alleged presence of Ukrainian Defense Forces in western Libya. President Volodymyr Zelensky referred to the strikes in an address to NATO lawmakers earlier on Monday, Nov. 23.

Not Admitting Ukraine to NATO in 2008 Was a Mistake, Merz Says — NATO allies made a mistake at the 2008 summit in Romania by not admitting Ukraine, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said on Monday, Nov. 23, arguing that membership might have prevented Russia’s full-scale invasion. Speaking alongside NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte in Berlin, Merz also backed French President Emmanuel Macron's call to reopen talks on Ukraine's accession and said Kyiv needs postwar guarantees close to Article 5.

Dymer Rescue Operation Concludes With 11 Dead — Search and rescue operations at a residential building in Dymer, Kyiv region, concluded on Monday, Nov. 23, after more than a day of work. The Russian drone strike on the five-story building killed 11 people, including an 11-year-old girl, while five remaining survivors were hospitalized. Rescuers pulled a 7-year-old boy and a 79-year-old woman alive from under the rubble.

Russia Reportedly Uses Discord, WhatsApp, Telegram to Recruit European Saboteurs — Ukraine’s military intelligence has accused Russian intelligence of using Telegram, WhatsApp and Discord to recruit for espionage and sabotage operations across the EU. Russian Military Supplier Arrested for Anti-Corruption Donations — Anton Linkvist, a military equipment store owner who once supplied clothes to GRU’s secretive Unit 92154, has been arrested for donating to late opposition leader Navalny’s FBK group. Linkvist is facing up to eight years in prison, though most of the accused have avoided jail time. Moscow is estimated to have raked in an estimated $527,000 in fines for a combined $5,270 in estimated donations.

NATO Membership Would Better Protect Ukraine, Zelensky Says — The Ukrainian leader told the NATO Parliamentary Assembly on Monday that admitting Ukraine would be cheaper and more reliable than security guarantees modeled on Article 5. He said Kyiv still lacked clear answers on who would respond to a new attack and at what cost. In separate remarks on Saturday, he said Ukraine had not yet received any written proposal for such guarantees.

Auterion, SkyFall Plan Drone Factory in Germany to Supply Ukraine — US drone software company Auterion and Ukrainian drone maker SkyFall have signed an agreement to form a joint venture that would build drones at a new factory in Germany, Auterion said on Friday. Russia Hits Repaired Odesa Power Lines, Zelensky Says — Russia is deliberately striking restored electricity lines and searching for alternative power supply routes to destroy in the Odesa region, the Ukrainian leader said. He specifically called for delays affecting US PAC-2 and PAC-3 Patriot interceptors to be overcome.

Why Russian Warship Sunk by Ukraine off Libyan Coast Regarded as Special — Ukraine’s strike on the Russian frigate Merkury in Libya destroyed one of Russia’s most advanced and expensive warships, equipped with sophisticated radar systems and a formidable missile arsenal. Kyiv Drone Attack Injures 5, Including US Citizen — Five people were injured and hospitalized following a Russian drone attack on Kyiv on Nov. 23, Mayor Vitalii Klitschko said in an updated statement. A fire spread to a residential building in Shevchenkivskyi district, while a drone struck a residential building’s roof in Podilskyi district.

Emergency blackouts remain in place in Kharkiv, while power restrictions continue nationwide.

Russia’s embassy rejected the allegations, while military officials warned that a nuclear detonation in orbit could cause widespread damage to satellite networks.

Four House races remain undecided. With Democrats also winning a 56-seat Senate majority, the incoming Congress will give the party greater power to challenge President Donald Trump’s policies when it takes office in January.
